items.stem: Which statement about the subset construction is correct?

options.text: It converts an NFA into an equivalent DFA whose states are sets of NFA states
options.rationale: Correct: DFA states correspond to subsets of NFA states reachable on an input.

options.text: It proves that NFAs recognise more languages than DFAs
options.rationale: Wrong: the construction shows they recognise exactly the same class.

options.text: It minimises the number of states in a DFA
options.rationale: Minimisation is a separate algorithm (e.g. Hopcroft's).

options.text: It only works for deterministic inputs
options.rationale: It is specifically for converting non-deterministic automata.

items.explanation: Correct: DFA states correspond to subsets of NFA states reachable on an input.

items.stem: Why does the pumping lemma help prove a language is NOT regular?

options.text: A regular language must allow long strings to be pumped; exhibiting a string that cannot be is a contradiction
options.rationale: Correct: it is used contrapositively to derive a contradiction.

options.text: It constructs the minimal DFA for the language
options.rationale: That is not what the lemma does.

options.text: It shows every context-free language is regular
options.rationale: False; CFLs are a strictly larger class.

options.text: It enumerates all strings the language accepts
options.rationale: The lemma is not an enumeration procedure.

items.explanation: Correct: it is used contrapositively to derive a contradiction.

items.stem: Which statements about the halting problem are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It is undecidable: no algorithm decides it for all inputs
options.rationale: Correct: Turing proved no total decider exists.

options.text: It is recognisable: a machine can accept all halting instances
options.rationale: Correct: simulate and accept if it halts, giving recognisability but not decidability.
False; it is not even decidable, so complexity classes like P do not apply.

options.text: It can be solved by a sufficiently large finite automaton
options.rationale: False; finite automata cannot even recognise it.

items.explanation: Correct: Turing proved no total decider exists.; Correct: simulate and accept if it halts, giving recognisability but not decidability.
